$\left(\begin{array}[]{l}\phantom{\Bigl(}\overline{t}_{21}^{(k)}\overline{t}_{12}^{(l)}\\
\phantom{\Bigl(}\overline{t}_{21}^{(k-1)}\overline{t}_{12}^{(l)}+\overline{t}_{21}^{(k)}\overline{t}_{12}^{(l-1)}\\
\phantom{\Bigl(}\overline{t}_{21}^{(k-2)}\overline{t}_{12}^{(l)}+\overline{t}_{21}^{(k-1)}\overline{t}_{12}^{(l-1)}+\overline{t}_{21}^{(k)}\overline{t}_{12}^{(l-2)}\\
\phantom{\Bigl(}\vdots\\
\phantom{\Bigl(}\overline{t}_{21}^{(k-a+1)}\overline{t}_{12}^{(l)}+\overline{t}_{21}^{(k-a+2)}\overline{t}_{12}^{(l+1)}+\cdots+\overline{t}_{21}^{(k)}\overline{t}_{12}^{(l-a+1)}\\
\end{array}\right)$

Note that when $k=l=a=p$ the rows of the table are exactly the elements $\nabla_{i}$, $i=p+1,\ldots,2p$. We will show by induction on $a$ that the sequence of rows of $s(k,l,a)$ is regular. Note that $s(k,l,1)$ consists of the single element $\overline{t}_{21}^{(k)}\overline{t}_{12}^{(l)}$ and is obviously regular. Now let $a>1$. Consider the following two tables which we denote by $s^{\prime}(k,l,a)$ and $s^{\prime\prime}(k,l,a)$, respectively.

$\left(\begin{array}[]{l}\phantom{\Bigl(}\overline{t}_{21}^{(k)}\\
\phantom{\Bigl(}\overline{t}_{21}^{(k-1)}\overline{t}_{12}^{(l)}+\overline{t}_{21}^{(k)}\overline{t}_{12}^{(l-1)}\\
\phantom{\Bigl(}\vdots\\
\phantom{\Bigl(}\overline{t}_{21}^{(k-a+1)}\overline{t}_{12}^{(l)}+\cdots+\overline{t}_{21}^{(k)}\overline{t}_{12}^{(l-a+1)}\\
\end{array}\right),\qquad\left(\begin{array}[]{l}\phantom{\Bigl(}\overline{t}_{12}^{(l)}\\
\phantom{\Bigl(}\overline{t}_{21}^{(k-1)}\overline{t}_{12}^{(l)}+\overline{t}_{21}^{(k)}\overline{t}_{12}^{(l-1)}\\
\phantom{\Bigl(}\vdots\\
\phantom{\Bigl(}\overline{t}_{21}^{(k-a+1)}\overline{t}_{12}^{(l)}+\cdots+\overline{t}_{21}^{(k)}\overline{t}_{12}^{(l-a+1)}\\
\end{array}\right)$

paper.title: Harish-Chandra modules for Yangians
paper.abstract: We study Harish-Chandra representations of Yangian for gl(2). We prove an analogue of Kostant theorem showing that resterited Yangians for gl(2) are free modules over certain maximal commutative subalgebras. We also study the categories of generic Harish-Chandra modules, describe their simple modules and indecomposable modules in tame blocks.
